headline: LeBron James has his 1st triple-double for the 76ers in a win over the Heat
text: PHILADELPHIA -- — LeBron James had 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double with Philadelphia, and Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points to lead the 76ers to a 111-104 victory over the Miami Heat in an NBA Cup game Wednesday night. Giannis Antetokounmpo had 32 points and 14 rebounds for Miami, and Davion Mitchell scored 20 points. The 76ers played a second straight game without Joel Embiid (illness), and Jaylen Brown was ruled out after the first half with left hamstring tightness . Brown missed two games last week because of the hamstring injury and hurt it again at the end of the second quarter. Brown, who scored six points, grabbed at his left hamstring, checked himself out the game and walked straight to the locker room. James did it all in their absence. Heat coach Erik Spoelstra coached James when the Heat won consecutive NBA championships in 2012 and 2013. Spoelstra said of James ahead of the game, "Father Time always wins. But right now, he’s giving Father Time hell.” James, who turns 42 on Dec. 30, brought it against Miami when he scored 14 straight points in the first half that gave the 76ers a 47-39 lead and sent the crowd into an absolute frenzy. James' run started simple enough with a three-point play. He buried one long 3, then ripped a longer one from the top of the arc for nine straight. His third 3, that was for show. James hit it from the left side and gave a little shrug. He bobbed his head and licked his lips as the Heat called a timeout and the “LeBron, LeBron, LeBron” remix song played in the arena. He powered down the lane for a layup for 14 straight points. Well shy of the 25 consecutive points he scored in a 2007 playoff game against Detroit. More than enough for the Sixers in a needed rebound victory after they allowed 19-pointers and were blown out by Portland on Monday. James capped his highlight reel with a ridiculous transition alley-oop pass from beyond halfcourt to VJ Edgecombe for a 98-84 lead. He grabbed his 10th rebound with 1:44 left to secure his first triple-double as a Sixer. Up next Heat: At New York on Friday night. 76ers: At Indiana on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Matas Buzelis scores 24 as Bulls hold on to beat Hornets 107-105 for 2nd straight win
text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Matas Buzelis scored 24 points, Josh Giddey added 12 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, and the Chicago Bulls handed the Charlotte Hornets their seventh straight loss 107-105 on Wednesday night. Tre Jones had 10 points and eight assists for the Bulls, who escaped with their second straight win when Coby White’s off-balance jumper rimmed out at the buzzer. Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 35 points, his fourth 30-point game of the season. Naz Reid had 18 points, while Moussa Diabate added 14 points and 14 rebounds for the Hornets, who shot 41% from the field. The game featured 22 lead changes, more than half of those in the fourth quarter. With the Bulls leading by one, Buzelis tipped in a weakside rebound with 23.2 seconds left to make it a 3-point game. Miller scored on a driving layup with 18.7 seconds left to cut the lead back to one, but Buzelis answered with two free throws with 10.1 seconds left to push the lead back to three. The Hornets wanted a 3 to tie, but Buzelis fouled White on the floor before he could get a shot off. White made two free throws with 8.8 seconds left to cut the lead back to one. White dove on the floor to deny a side inbounds pass on Chicago's next possession, but was whistled for a foul. Jones missed the first of two free throws with 8.5 seconds left but made the second. Without any timeouts left, the Hornets inbounded the ball and White drove the length of the floor before launching a leaning 15-foot jumper from the right side that missed. The Bulls wrapped up NBA group play with a 2-2 record, while the Hornets finished 0-4. Charlotte led 48-46 at halftime despite shooting 36% from the field and 21% from beyond the arc. Up next Bulls: Host Pacers on Saturday night. Hornets: Host Nets on Saturday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Knicks blow by the Cavaliers in the fourth, win 121-102 for sixth straight victory
text: NEW YORK -- — Jose Alvarado scored a season-high 21 points, Mikal Bridges had a season-best 19 and the New York Knicks rode a blitz by their bench to a 121-102 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night that extended their winning streak to six. Jalen Brunson also scored 19, but the Knicks captain, who was questionable earlier in the day with an illness, labored to a 6-for-22 shooting night and the Knicks fell behind by 11 points multiple times. It was Alvarado, his backup, who was on the floor when the Knicks blew by the Cavaliers to start the fourth quarter. Josh Hart had 15 points, 12 assists and seven rebounds, and Karl-Anthony Towns finished with 12 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists, barely extending his season-opening streak to 17 consecutive games with a double-double. The defending champion Knicks would have been eliminated from NBA Cup title contention with a loss but outscored the Cavs 39-17 in the fourth on their blue court with orange lining the outside. Donovan Mitchell scored 30 points and James Harden had 28 for the Cavaliers, who fell to 9-10. Both teams were without their top defensive forwards, with the Knicks' OG Anunoby sidelined by a strained left calf and Cleveland's Evan Mobley still out with a toe injury. New York was also without key reserves Deuce McBride (left adductor tightness) and Jordan Clarkson (right plantar fasciitis), and lost backup center Andre Drummond to a head injury during the game. The Cavaliers led by 11 with under four minutes remaining in the first half. They went back ahead by 11 in the third quarter but the Knicks had it down to 85-82 headed to the fourth, then surged into the lead when Alvarado made consecutive 3-pointers for a 90-85 lead. Pacome Dadiet , another backup, then had consecutive baskets on the break, and after a Cleveland 3-pointer, Bridges scored and Alvarado made another 3 and suddenly it was the Knicks with an 11-point lead. When third-string center James Wiseman had consecutive baskets, the Knicks had outscored the Cavs 25-9 to start the fourth and had a 107-94 lead. Up next Cavaliers: Host Miami on Sunday. Knicks: Host Miami on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Timberwolves beat the Thunder 113-106 to improve to 3-0 in NBA Cup play
text: OKLAHOMA CITY -- — Jaden McDaniels had 32 points and 10 rebounds, LaMelo Ball added 19 points before leaving with an ankle injury and the Minnesota Timberwolves improved to 3-0 in NBA Cup play with a 113-106 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday night. Ball left the game in the the final 2:30 after landing on the foot of Thunder center Isaiah Hartenstein while they were fighting for a rebound. Minnesota made 17 of 39 3-pointers (43.6%) and outrebounded the short-handed Thunder 40-30. Oklahoma City was playing without injured 7-foot-3 rookie Aday Mara (shin contusion). McDaniels made 11 of 15 shots and was four of five from beyond the arc for the Timberwolves (14-5), who have won 10 of their last 12 games. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 points and Ajay Mitchell added 25 for the Thunder (10-9), who have dropped six of nine amid the loss of three starters to long-term injuries. Oklahoma City overcame a poor-shooting first quarter by outscoring the Timberwolves 37-21 in the second for a 53-47 halftime lead. Gilgeous-Alexander had 12 points in the quarter, including nine in the final three minutes. The advantage grew to 73-63 on a 3-point play by SGA, but Minnesota responded with a 24-10 run to close out the third quarter. McDaniels made a pair of shots from distance, including a 26-footer at the buzzer to put the Timberwolves in front 87-83. Oklahoma City pulled to within 105-104 on a 3-pointer by Mitchell but could not get any closer after that. Up next Timberwolves: Host Memphis on Friday night. Thunder: Play at Milwaukee on Saturday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Wells and Jerome lead the Grizzlies to a 115-97 win over the Clippers, who fall to 0-9 on the road
text: MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- — Jaylen Wells scored 19 points, Ty Jerome added 17 points and seven assists, and the Memphis Grizzles beat the Clippers 115-70 on Wednesday night in an NBA Cup game, dropping Los Angeles to 0-9 on the road. The Clippers finished their current trip at 0-4, with each loss by at least 10 points. They are the only NBA team without a road win this season. Cam Spencer scored 16 points and Cedric Coward finished with 14 points and 10 rebounds for Memphis, which has won seven of eight. The Grizzlies will meet the Timberwolves on Friday for the top spot in West Group B. Brandon Ingram , who made his first appearance of the season in Monday's loss at Houston, led the Clippers with 18 points. Ingram missed LA's first 15 games with a right heel injury. Rui Hachimura had 14 points and 12 rebounds, and Darius Garland , rookie Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn finished with 12 points each. Memphis built an early 20-point lead as the Clippers struggled from the field. The shooting got better for Los Angeles, which trailed 50-43 at the half. The teams — tops in the league from 3-point range — were a combined 8 of 37 from beyond the arc in the first half. That included the starting Grizzlies backcourt of Coward and Jerome missing all 11 of their 3-point attempts. The Clippers turned it into a one-possession game early in the third, but Memphis responded with an 18-2 run. Los Angeles never got closer than 13 in the fourth. Up next Clippers: Host New Orleans on Friday. Grizzlies: At Minnesota on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Randle scores 28 points to lead Nets past Bucks 104-97 in NBA Cup action
text: MILWAUKEE -- — Julius Randle scored 28 points and Noah Clowney had 17 as the Brooklyn Nets beat the Milwaukee Bucks 104-97 to snap a five-game losing streak on Wednesday night in NBA Cup play. Egor Demin added 15, Michael Porter Jr . had 12 points and 11 rebounds and Day’Ron Sharpe chipped in with 11 points and 14 rebounds for Brooklyn, which improved to 1-2 in NBA Cup group play. Tyler Herro scored 28 points, Jaime Jaquez Jr . had 21 and Kyle Kuzma and Kel’el Ware 13 apiece for the Bucks, who fell to 0-3 in the NBA Cup group that also includes Detroit, Orlando and Toronto. The Bucks, who snapped a 13-game losing streak by beating the Toronto Raptors 116-111 on Monday night, jumped out to a 9-2 first-quarter lead but the Nets countered with a 16-2 run to pull ahead. Brooklyn led 28-24 after the opening period. The Nets built a 13-point lead in the second quarter and led 51-47 at the half after a late Bucks push. Randle had 16 first-half points while Sharpe had 10 rebounds. Milwaukee took a 56-55 lead on Herro's 3-pointer early in the third and led by six in the quarter, but Brooklyn regained control and led 76-71 headed to the fourth. The Nets, who were routed by the Minnesota Timberwolves 142-116 on Monday night, pushed the lead to double digits in the final period and held off the Bucks down the stretch. Nets center Moe Wagner departed with left knee soreness. Up next Nets: At Toronto on Friday night. Bucks: At Detroit on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Kevin Durant reaches 33,000 points as Rockets beat Suns
text: HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant scored 20 points and became the fifth player in NBA history to reach 33,000 points, helping the Houston Rockets beat the Phoenix Suns 116-104 on Wednesday night. Durant shot 7 of 15 from the field and grabbed 10 rebounds. A three-pointer with 46.3 seconds left in the second quarter put him in the 33,000-point club with LeBron James , Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant. The Suns (9-8) had a four-game winning streak end and were eliminated them from NBA Cup contention. Houston (14-5) was eliminated Tuesday night when Dallas defeated Denver. The Mavericks advanced to the knockout round by winning West Group A. Alperen Sengun finished with 23 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists for his third triple-double of the season. Amen Thompson added 18 points and 10 rebounds for Houston. Devin Booker led the Suns with 25 points. Phoenix made just five 3s and connected on just 1 of its last 24 attempts. The Rockets closed the first half on a 12-5 run to take a 66-56 lead into halftime. The Suns started the fourth quarter with a 16-5 burst to pull within two, but Fred VanVleet drained a 3 from the right corner to stop the bleeding. VanVleet added another 3 to increase the lead to 10. Up next Rockets: Host Philadelphia on Saturday night. Suns: Host Dallas on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NHL coverage here

headline: De'Anthony Melton scores 24 points, matches career high with eight 3s as Warriors beat Kings 129-110
text: SAN FRANCISCO -- — De'Anthony Melton scored 24 points and matched his career high with eight 3-pointers and the Golden State Warriors made 20 total 3s on the way to a 129-110 win over the Sacramento Kings in an NBA Cup game on Wednesday night. Gui Santos scored 22 points off the bench for Golden State as the reserves contributed a season-best 61 points. Melton shot 8 for 14 in his third 20-point performance of the season and added seven assists. Golden State had 37 assists and improved to 2-4 during this recent stretch without Stephen Curry , who is scheduled to be re-evaluated Friday after missing two weeks with a torn right oblique abdominal muscle. Charles Bassey had 10 points and seven rebounds in Golden State's second consecutive win after the Warriors beat the Boston Celtics 88-87 on Sunday to snap a five-game losing streak. Sacramento (2-16) had also held off the Celtics by one point a night earlier for just its second win and first at home. Domantas Sabonis had 27 points, 10 rebounds and six assists, rookie Darius Acuff Jr . added 22 points and nine assists and Keegan Murray added 18 points for the Kings. Emanuel Sharp 's 3-pointer with 4:34 left in the third pulled Sacramento within 85-81 only for Will Richard to make a baseline 3 moments later. The Warriors hit seven of their initial eight 3-pointers to take a 33-16 lead — 44-19 after the opening quarter for their most points in any period this season — and wound up 20 for 44 from long range. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 15 points and eight rebounds as Golden State matched its most points in a first half with 72. Golden State's Brandon Williams returned from a six-game absence because of a strained left hamstring and had 14 points and three assists in 12 minutes. Up next Kings: Host the Timberwolves on Sunday night. Warriors: Visit Portland on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Avdija, Lillard lead Trail Blazers to 116-111 win over Spurs in NBA Cup play
text: PORTLAND, Ore. -- — Deni Avdija scored 33 points to lead the Portland Trail Blazers to a 116-111 win over the San Antonio Spurs in both teams’ third NBA Cup matchup of the group stage on Wednesday. Damian Lillard added 29 points for the Blazers (12-6) to go along with 16 from Sidy Cissoko . Jrue Holiday had 11 points off the bench while Scoot Henderson had 10. Victor Wembanyama led all scorers with 44 points on 17 of 30 shooting for the Spurs (16-4), along with 16 rebounds and two blocks. Stephon Castle added 20 points, six rebounds and nine assists, while Devin Vassell had 18 points. The win keeps the Blazers alive for a wild-card spot in the knockout round, where they’re now 2-1 in group play with a +7 point differential. San Antonio leads their group with a differential of +48. Both teams play their final group-stage matchup on Friday. Up next Spurs: At Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night. Trail Blazers: Host Golden State at on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
